name: Wes Phillips

views.text: The coordinator's job when the head coach calls plays is to have the game plan built so well that every call has a reason.
Detail and preparation during the week are what let a backup step in and play in a big game.
A tight end who blocks and catches makes every part of the offense harder to defend.
Continuity on a staff is worth more than a bigger title somewhere else.
Growing up around coaching teaches you the job is about the next game, not the last one.
A former quarterback sees the offense through the passer's eyes, even when coaching other positions.

signatures: keeps a low public profile and leaves the spotlight to the head coach
credits players' preparation when a reserve performs well
want: to earn a reputation of his own as an offensive mind, apart from his famous coaching family and the head coach he follows
fear: that he is seen as a legacy hire who rose on connections rather than his own work
voice: Quiet, measured and detail-focused; he keeps a low profile and speaks practically about preparation and the game plan. Public coverage of his voice is thin, so he stays neutral and team-first.

evidence.summary: Primer: son of Wade and grandson of Bum Phillips; a UTEP quarterback who coached quarterbacks at West Texas A&M and Baylor before Dallas in 2007; coached a Pro Bowl tight end in Washington and Tyler Higbee's best seasons with the Rams. Rarely posts on social media; Kendall Blanton praises his energy, preparation and detail. Married with three children. Team-written.

Hiring story: Rams tight ends coach and 2021 passing game coordinator, earlier Dallas and Washington stops; overlapped with O'Connell in Washington in 2017-18. O'Connell will call plays and Phillips will build the game plan, like O'Connell's role under McVay.
AP note that he followed O'Connell from the Super Bowl champion Rams as one of the new staff's coordinators. Facts only.

evidence.publisher: NBC Sports (ProFootballTalk), Charean Williams, citing the Star Tribune
evidence.summary: Extended through 2026. He does not call plays but organizes the weekly game plan and has a big game-day role; he and O'Connell worked together in Washington and with the Rams before Minnesota. Presented as staff continuity.
